topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, audience, and core learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Cellular, developmental, and experimental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a disease driven by accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and 3D tissue architecture, alongside the methods and challenges of modeling these behaviors in culture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained benign growths to locally invasive and distant metastatic malignancies, illustrating the morphological and histological criteria used to identify these transitions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature, clinical risks, and mechanisms of morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the naming conventions for different tumor types and explain how benign and malignant neoplasms cause physiological dysfunction, morbidity, and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the incidence and mortality of various tumor types in humans and examine how cancer manifests across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical cancer screening and diagnostic modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the rationale, histological foundations, and practical utility of population-level screening approaches across major cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture closing and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of learning outcomes and practical session reminders.
